title: CostClaw: local Claude Code token estimates
excerpt: A local Claude Code audit with dated list-price estimates, counterfactual cache exposure, and rule-based setup scores. Prompts stay local.
content_html:
Local audit for Claude Code

See where your Claude Code spend leaks.

CostClaw reads the Claude Code logs already on your disk, estimates token value from current list prices, and scores your setup across six rule-based pillars. It analyzes prompts locally and never uploads them.

npx costclaw audit

See what it finds

No account, no upload. It parses the logs on your disk and prints a report.

The leak

Logs show scenarios. Your invoice is the billing record.

CostClaw reads session logs on your disk, including subagent and workflow sub-logs, and compares logged token use with scenarios worth investigating. It does not reconcile an invoice or guarantee savings. Four signals it shows:

input  $3.00 / MTok cache read  $0.30 / MTok

Cache-miss exposure

Claude Code caches the front of your prompt so repeat tokens cost a tenth of the price. When a session rebuilds that cache instead of reusing it, you pay full input rate on tokens that should have been lower-priced. CostClaw estimates that counterfactual gap from logged fields.

Read ×142 in one session

Reactive tool loops

A session that fires the same tool a hundred times is usually thrashing: re-reading, re-grepping, circling a problem. It does not show up as a line item, but it burns tokens and time. CostClaw counts the loops and flags the sessions that run hot.

Opus  $15 / MTok Sonnet  $3 / MTok

Model misrouting

A short, simple session does not need the top model. When a quick task runs on Opus that might have been suitable for a cheaper model, CostClaw flags it for review. It does not determine task quality or guarantee a cheaper model would succeed.

cache  91% 34% by the last turns

Sessions that outgrow the cache

A session that runs for hours keeps adding context until the cache stops paying off. The early turns hit it; the closing turns re-pay full price for a prompt that only grew. CostClaw tracks the per-turn cache and flags sessions that may benefit from compaction.

How it works

Three passes over logs you already have.

  1. 1

    Parse locally

    It reads the JSONL session logs under your Claude directory, including the subagent and workflow sub-logs, in memory, on your machine. Nothing is sent anywhere.

  2. 2

    Derive a summary

    It analyzes raw logs locally to derive dated list-price estimates by reported model, cache hit rate per turn, tool use, and session timing. Prompts, paths, and code are dropped from the output.

  3. 3

    Score and rank

    It applies rules to six setup pillars and ranks counterfactual opportunities. The report prints to your terminal; estimates are not invoice totals or guaranteed savings.

How CostClaw estimates value and where the estimate stops

Method. For each accepted logged request, CostClaw applies the dated API list price for its reported model and sums input, output, cache-write, and cache-read token fields. A synthetic 1,000,000-token one-hour Sonnet cache write is valued at $6.00. Repeated cumulative updates are deduplicated so the latest observed total is counted once.

Scope. The report can use logged cache TTL splits when present. If a valid top-level cache-write count conflicts with a nested split, it preserves that count, estimates it at the conservative one-hour rate, and warns. Legacy writes with no split use the five-minute rate with a warning. It cannot establish model provenance, provider discounts, every billing modifier, subscription inclusion, or an Anthropic invoice total.

Interpretation. Cache-miss exposure compares logged usage with a cache-read counterfactual. In a synthetic mixed-model case, the list-price estimate is $0.10001 and the exposure is $0.090009. That is a scenario to investigate, not recoverable money or a quota guarantee. Setup scores are rule-based signals, not provider grades.

What you get

One command. Four answers.

A dated list-price estimate, with its limits

Estimated API-equivalent value over the window you audit, your cache hit rate, and a cache-miss counterfactual. It is based on logged fields and current list prices, not an invoice or a promise of savings.

List-price estimate

Cache hit

Cache-miss scenario

A six-pillar setup score from evidence

CLAUDE.md quality, context hygiene, prompting, session management, tooling, and cost discipline. Scores are rule-based signals from the logs, settings, and CLAUDE.md available to the audit. A pillar with no evidence reads n/a; it is not a provider quality grade.

  • Context hygiene50
  • Cost discipline67
  • Session management100

Opportunities ranked by estimated exposure

The list leads with the largest modeled scenario and its evidence, then suggests a change to review. Dollar figures are counterfactual estimates, not money promised back.

  • $90.01 Investigate cache-miss exposure
  • $0.00 Use a cheaper model for small sessions
  • warn Workflow and subagent runs add up

The week your spend actually follows

Burn Clock buckets every dollar by local day and time of day, so you can see the rhythm the bill hides. The peak day is compared against an average day, never against your quietest hour, so the multiplier stays a number you can check against the bars. Under seven active days it reads n/a instead of guessing a pattern.

  • Exa $100.01

Synthetic example only: one day with $100.01 in estimated API-equivalent value. Real reports omit a pattern when there is insufficient activity.

Privacy as the moat

Checkable, not just promised.

The audit saves a derived AuditRecord with totals and generated sentences. Raw prompt text and path markers are covered by privacy tests that run in the build.

The test plants tripwire strings, a fake prompt and a fake client path, into sample logs, runs the full pipeline, and asserts that none of them appear in the record. The build fails if any tested private marker survives.

content_html_zh:
克劳德代码的本地审核

See where your Claude Code spend leaks.

CostClaw reads the Claude Code logs already on your disk, estimates token value from current list prices, and scores your setup across six rule-based pillars. It analyzes prompts locally and never uploads them.

npx costclaw 审计

See what it finds

没有帐号，无法上传。 它解析磁盘上的日志并打印报告。

泄漏

Logs show scenarios. Your invoice is the billing record.

CostClaw reads session logs on your disk, including subagent and workflow sub-logs, and compares logged token use with scenarios worth investigating. It does not reconcile an invoice or guarantee savings. Four signals it shows:

输入 $3.00 / MTok 缓存读取 $0.30 / MTok

缓存未命中暴露

Claude Code 会缓存提示符的前面部分，因此重复令牌的价格仅为十分之一。 When a session rebuilds that cache instead of reusing it, you pay full input rate on tokens that should have been lower-priced. CostClaw estimates that counterfactual gap from logged fields.

一节阅读×142

反应式工具循环

触发同一个工具一百次的会话通常会造成混乱：重新阅读、重新 grep、圈出问题。 它不会显示为订单项，但会消耗代币和时间。 CostClaw 对循环进行计数并标记运行热点的会话。

作品 $15 / MTok 十四行诗 $3 / MTok

模型错误路由

简短的会话不需要顶级模型。 When a quick task runs on Opus that might have been suitable for a cheaper model, CostClaw flags it for review. It does not determine task quality or guarantee a cheaper model would succeed.

最后一轮缓存 91% 34%

超出缓存范围的会话

运行数小时的会话会不断添加上下文，直到缓存停止发挥作用。 早期的转弯击中了它；收盘时轮流偿还全价，以换取不断增长的提示。 CostClaw tracks the per-turn cache and flags sessions that may benefit from compaction.

它是如何运作的

对您已有的日志进行三遍。

  1. 1 本地解析 它读取计算机内存中 Claude 目录下的 JSONL 会话日志，包括子代理和工作流子日志。 没有任何东西被发送到任何地方。
  2. 2 Derive a summary It analyzes raw logs locally to derive dated list-price estimates by reported model, cache hit rate per turn, tool use, and session timing. Prompts, paths, and code are dropped from the output.
  3. 3 Score and rank It applies rules to six setup pillars and ranks counterfactual opportunities. The report prints to your terminal; estimates are not invoice totals or guaranteed savings.
How CostClaw estimates value and where the estimate stops

Method. For each accepted logged request, CostClaw applies the dated API list price for its reported model and sums input, output, cache-write, and cache-read token fields. A synthetic 1,000,000-token one-hour Sonnet cache write is valued at $6.00. Repeated cumulative updates are deduplicated so the latest observed total is counted once.

范围。 The report can use logged cache TTL splits when present. If a valid top-level cache-write count conflicts with a nested split, it preserves that count, estimates it at the conservative one-hour rate, and warns. Legacy writes with no split use the five-minute rate with a warning. It cannot establish model provenance, provider discounts, every billing modifier, subscription inclusion, or an Anthropic invoice total.

Interpretation. Cache-miss exposure compares logged usage with a cache-read counterfactual. In a synthetic mixed-model case, the list-price estimate is $0.10001 and the exposure is $0.090009. That is a scenario to investigate, not recoverable money or a quota guarantee. Setup scores are rule-based signals, not provider grades.
